title: US Signs $2.45B in Non-Chinese Tungsten Deals, Senate Probes Vance Over Vitol Venezuela Oil Contract, and SpaceX Lands $24B Texas Data Center Permit
subhead: Washington locked in multibillion-dollar supply contracts to replace Chinese tungsten before a January Pentagon ban, Senate investigators opened an inquiry into Vice President JD Vance's alleged pre-war contact with oil trader Vitol, and surging AI power demand reshaped North American and Central Asian grids.

sections.heading: Washington Commits $2.45 Billion to Non-Chinese Tungsten Supply Ahead of Pentagon Ban
sections.body:
OilPrice reports that the United States government has signed supply and financing agreements worth up to $2.45 billion this year to secure non-Chinese sources of tungsten ahead of a strict Defense Department procurement ban taking effect on January 1, 2027. Under the statutory restriction, defense contractors will be barred from delivering weapons components containing tungsten mined, refined, or separated in China, Russia, Iran, or North Korea.

The scramble highlights the steep capital inflation hitting Western critical-mineral reshoring. Separate project filings cited by OilPrice show that the Trump administration's flagship domestic lithium extraction venture now faces a 31 percent cost overrun above initial engineering estimates due to chemical processing equipment bottlenecks, high interest rates, and skilled-labor shortages across US mining states.
sections.whyItMatters: Legislating hard cutoffs on Chinese critical minerals is far faster than building Western refining capacity, forcing Washington to underwrite multibillion-dollar offtake guarantees and absorb double-digit capital overruns to avoid munitions and battery bottlenecks.

sections.heading: US Senate Opens Investigation Into JD Vance's Alleged Ties to Vitol Venezuela Oil Deal
sections.body:
OilPrice and Reuters report that the US Senate has launched a formal investigation into alleged contacts between Vice President JD Vance and Swiss-Dutch commodities trading giant Vitol concerning a lucrative Venezuelan crude-marketing contract. Senate investigators are examining disclosures following an earlier Reuters report alleging that Vance met privately with a senior Vitol oil trader prior to US military intervention in Venezuela.

Lawmakers are seeking records from both the Vice President's office and federal licensing authorities to determine whether preferential trading allocations or sanctions waivers were discussed ahead of sovereign control shifts over Venezuelan heavy-crude exports. Venezuelan barrels remain prized by US Gulf Coast refineries configured to process heavy sour grades into middle distillates at a time when global diesel inventories remain tight.
sections.whyItMatters: Congressional scrutiny of the Vitol arrangement puts political and legal risk directly onto post-intervention Venezuelan crude marketing, threatening to complicate Gulf Coast heavy-sour refinery slates if trading licenses are frozen or revised.

sections.heading: SpaceX Secures $24B Texas Starbase Data Center Permit as Central Asia Pilots Unified Power Market
sections.body:
OilPrice and Politico report that the first major data-center permit issued by Texas regulators after lifting a statewide grid-connection freeze went to SpaceX for a proposed $24 billion computing complex at Starbase. Meanwhile, Environment+Energy Leader reports that developers unveiled the Texas Gateway natural gas transmission expansion to move additional Permian and Haynesville volumes toward Gulf Coast power generators and LNG terminals, even as Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney courted foreign capital with bundled LNG, mining, and data-center packages.

Grid integration is also advancing across Eurasia, where OilPrice reports that Kazakhstan's state grid operator KEGOC launched a World Bank-backed tender for a 24-month pilot establishing a regional Central Asian electricity market. In the United Kingdom, however, BBC reports that energy regulator Ofgem is raising its January household price cap, confronting millions of British consumers with sharply higher winter domestic gas bills.
sections.whyItMatters: Pairing multi-gigawatt hyperscale compute clusters like SpaceX's $24 billion Starbase project with dedicated gas infrastructure shows that data-center siting is now dictated primarily by firm thermal generation and regulatory fast-tracking.

sections.heading: WHO Demands End to US Fuel Blockade on Cuba as Power Shortfalls Paralyze Healthcare
sections.body:
Al Jazeera reports that the World Health Organization called for an immediate end to the United States fuel blockade on Cuba, warning that acute shortages of imported fuel oil and diesel are crippling electricity generation across hospitals, water pumping stations, and pharmaceutical storage facilities. The United Nations released $2 million in emergency funds to sustain vaccine refrigeration and essential medical gear as rolling blackouts deepen across Havana and provincial cities.

Cuba's aging oil-fired thermoelectric plants depend heavily on imported heavy crude and diesel cargoes that have dwindled sharply under tightened US maritime interdiction and secondary sanctions against shipping insurers, leaving backup hospital generators without steady fuel allocations.
sections.whyItMatters: The WHO intervention highlights the humanitarian threshold of maritime energy interdiction: cutting fuel deliveries to an import-dependent island grid rapidly cascades from transport rationing into systemic public-health failure.

sections.heading: Brent Sinks Below $90 on Libyan Pipeline Restart Despite Cyberattacks on Dozens of Tankers
sections.body:
OilPrice and Anadolu Agency report that Brent crude fell below $90 per barrel this week — extending a November slide of more than 20 percent — as the reopening of Libyan oil pipelines and expectations of a first-quarter global supply surplus outweighed ongoing Gulf maritime hostilities. American Petroleum Institute data showed US commercial crude inventories edging up by 126,000 barrels in the week ending November 20 following a 5.3 million barrel build the prior week, pushing US retail gasoline averages down toward $3.64 per gallon.

Yet physical and digital threats to maritime energy transport continue to mount. TechCrunch reports that cybersecurity investigators identified dozens of oil and chemical tankers hacked in recent weeks in a campaign attributed primarily to Iranian-linked actors, adding shipboard navigation and operational-technology compromises to the mine and drone hazards already facing Gulf shipping.
sections.whyItMatters: Brent's retreat below $90 despite tanker cyberattacks and Gulf missile strikes proves that physical barrel returns from Libya and rising non-OPEC supply are currently overpowering geopolitical risk premiums in paper oil markets.

bottomLine: Energy and mineral security are bifurcating along clear structural lines: crude oil prices are softening below $90 on returning Libyan supply and ample inventories, yet the physical inputs for defense and AI — from non-Chinese tungsten and domestic lithium to firm Texas gigawatts — face severe cost inflation and political bottlenecks.
sources: OilPrice, Reuters, Politico, Anadolu Agency, Al Jazeera, BBC, TechCrunch, Environment+Energy Leader
